cases.name: Michele "Luna" Jackson
cases.about:
She was a junior at Southeast Valley High School.

People said Jackson loved to visit the library. Library director Rebecca Slawson said she was at the library nearly every day it was open. She said there is a hole at the library now without her.

"It's really hard to be in here now when she's not here," Slawson said. "It's hard because she was so young. It's hard because it's somebody that I got to know and really care about."

Slawson said the two spent a lot of time talking about the future, like how Jackson wanted to study meteorology at Iowa State University or how excited Jackson was for the library's Comic-Con.

Slawson said she is still thinking of ways they could honor Jackson at the library. She wants to make sure her memory is kept alive there.

"We've discussed maybe getting an indoor succulent garden," Slawson said. "I would really like to have some manga. That was another one of her passions."

Most of all, Slawson said she hopes people will learn to see the library through Jackson's eyes: as a place to learn about things and learn about others.

"I want us to have the time to talk and really hear what each other has to say, get to know each other," she said.
cases.narrative: On 9/23/2024, her body was found at the Farnhamville City Park. He allegedly slit her throat. Jackson was reported missing Sunday night by her mother when she didn’t return from her nightly visit to the park. Her body was found Monday morning.
